biological_question: Among same-fine-pigment-state Petunieae species, can ancestry improve out-of-species prediction of each preassigned functional gene module beyond the full pigment-class expression mean? Do modules with phylogenetic distance association have operational predictive utility?

heldout_prediction.target: log1p raw expression TPM10K of each of the 21 published pathway-gene columns, for one withheld species; do NOT fit global per-gene z-scores including the withheld species
heldout_prediction.available_features_to_predict: six-bit measured pigment-presence class is treated as already known at prediction time; avoid claims of unguided floral phenotype prediction
heldout_prediction.baseline: For each held-out source species, average log1p gene expressions of ALL remaining species with the same exact six-bit source pigment class
heldout_prediction.ancestry_aware: For each held-out species, select k=2 nearest other tips on original dated source tree STRICTLY within the same six-bit pigment class, break patristic ties by original source tip name, and predict mean log1p expression of those two donors
heldout_prediction.module_loss: Per held-out taxon take mean squared prediction errors over ALL genes in each fixed module, scaling every gene error by the other 46 species' training-only log1p gene expression variance (same existing full 21-gene source fold standardization); then average equally over all 47 heldout taxa
heldout_prediction.module_gain: (module baseline MSE - module k=2 nearest MSE)/module baseline MSE, relative gain > 0 means concrete improvement over class mean

null.whole_vector_within_class: Permute intact original 21-gene expression vectors among the frozen 47 taxon labels only within their original six-bit pigment-presence code; hold source tree, six-bit labels and original k=2/class-mean donor weight matrices fixed. Each draw recomputes all 3 module fold-scaled gains from permuted training-only values, preserving multigene covariance.
null.nominal_upper_tail_p: (1 + number of simulated module gains >= observed gain) / 10000
null.adjusted_p: Apply Holm step-down correction to the three precommitted module locality null P values; this controls arbitrary dependence of the three family tests and does NOT make modules independent radiations.
null.success_rule: SUPPORTED_MODULE_TRANSFER only when observed practical module gain > 0 and Holm-adjusted locality upper-tail p <=0.05. If gain <=0, label NOT_SUPPORTED_PRACTICAL_TRANSFER even when permutation P is small.
null.hypothesis_direction: practical transfer must improve over pigment-class mean, not merely outperform the null's expected k2 overfitting
null.null_interpretation: Taxon-shuffle test asks whether the k=2 donor method beats an exchangeable within-pigment-class assignment. Because module prediction is computed after observing the whole-gene outcome in the same source, any apparently positive module would remain exploratory.

additional_descriptive.source_random_two_baseline: Exact mean of all distinct random-two same-class donor pairs' losses for each heldout taxon (no sampling): report nearest-two vs random-two improvement for context, not as a substitute for pigment-class-mean baseline.
additional_descriptive.per_class_diagnostics: Within each of six frozen classes, report species count and relative module losses/gains; no class-based rescue or P values.
additional_descriptive.module_effect_contrast: Show raw difference in normalized held-out gains between modules, explicitly NO formal significant comparison, no transfer into nested-memory decay rates.
additional_descriptive.fixed_pair_frame: Predictors and original 47 taxa are used unchanged; not new independent radiations.
